title: Remarks at the banquet, Dubuque, Iowa
paragraphs: I can say, and not merely in a diplomatic spirit, that I have thoroughly enjoyed this evening. It has been a great pleasure to visit your beautiful city.

I would like now to bear testimony to the way in which I have found the representatives of Iowa at the national capital approach questions of public interest. I have been able to ask both your Senators and Representatives for their aid in dealing with matters of moment to the nation. As a whole I have found them interested in questions of public policy; and I have found that they could guide, and counsel, and aid me in the matters that I deemed of moment to the nation at large, and that they were not merely bound by fourth class post offices. How I have felt toward your people I think it hardly needful for me to say. When I came to choose that member of my Cabinet who occupies the position which taken year in and year out is of most vital consequence to the welfare of the nation, I felt that although I should not ordinarily care to take two men from the same state, yet that Mr. Shaw's qualifications for the position were so preeminent that in justice to the nation I could not pass him by. (Cheers and applause)

As for Secretary Wilson, (Cheers and applause) after having been with him for twenty-one months, and after having been intimately associated with various different national administrations and knowing many members of the Cabinet, I wish to state without reserve that in point of loyalty, of that probity which makes one feel that one is better for being associated with him, that in point of sound common sense, not always a common quality, and in capacity to handle his office in the way that one would wish all offices of the government to be handled, if one could have ideal conditions, I have never met any man in public life who I feel quite came up to Secretary Wilson. (Cheers and applause) I cannot overstate the degree to [?] which I lean on him and the personal affection that I feel for him. (Applause)
In thanking you for the reception accorded me here in your city, let me also say how much I have enjoyed the dinner.
